apps.description:
Distro is the Detroit Automation Academy's native application-store app for macOS High Sierra: it browses the Academy catalog, downloads Academy-maintained apps from the AutomatedTechnologies GitHub org, verifies every download by SHA-256 before install, and carries no privileged helper. Prepared at DAADV3 T1 codification (2026-11-07); not yet published — publication remains gated on Distro tranche D-T5. Disassembled. Scanned. Recompiled. Distro distributes only apps carrying the Academy audit entry in their plist — proof of the Academy pipeline. distro-test-17 applies the SDS-9 liquid-glass cues to the store chrome: layered tint depth, the glass hairline pair on the dividers and sheet edges, capsule state controls, and the status word in a capsule chip — flat tints only, no behavior change.

© 2026 Detroit Automation Academy / Automated Technologies. All rights reserved. Detroit Automation Academy, Automated Technologies, Distro, Workbench, Live Transit Detroit, The Signal, and the Academy monochrome logo are marks of the Academy, used under the founder's permission. Academy-original works are licensed under the Academy License (revocable); upstream open-source components remain under their own licenses. distro-test-22 adds Update All: when updates are pending, one button runs them sequentially — each app still verified by SHA-256 and the audit gate on its own — and ends with a single summary. The detail pane now shows build notes for the catalog version and the installed app's file path. Catalog fetches now bypass HTTP caches, so Refresh always returns the current catalog.
apps.name: Distro
apps.tagline: The Academy's application store for High Sierra — browse, install, and update Academy apps.
apps.buildNotes: Pre-flight installs (charter section 6): before Distro places an update, it closes the app if it is running — politely first, force-quit only if the app does not quit, and the install stops untouched if the app still will not quit — and removes the previous version's bundle. Your app data is stored separately from the bundle and is never deleted or moved by an install, so settings and history carry across every update. An app that replaced an earlier product under a different name can declare its predecessor identities, and pre-flight treats a running predecessor and its bundle the same way. Everything else stands: SHA-256 verification and the audit gate in DistroInstaller still run before pre-flight, so an unverified download never disturbs a running app; the unified registered logo, the version read from the bundle on the welcome screen, the functional menu bar, and academy-distro:// deep links all carry over.

apps.buildNotes: Minion 0.4.3 — the avatar-CPU fix. Earlier builds let the hosted page's looping avatar animation decode and composite at full rate forever: on the owner's MacBook Air it measured roughly half the machine's CPU with the app simply open (Tachometer budget for the avatar: renderer + GPU at or under 10% of one thread sustained). 0.4.3 adds an avatar governor to the shell: the page's animation pauses — CSS animations held, video elements paused — whenever the page is hidden, the window is not frontmost, or the app sits idle for 45 seconds, and resumes the moment you click, type, or a reply starts streaming. While you are working in the app, the avatar animates exactly as before. Every 0.4.2 property stands, including the sign-in repair (an earlier build's sign-in carries into this one; a sign-in made inside 0.4.1's own separate session store is not read). Nothing about the app's name or surfaces changes: bundle Minion.app under com.detroitautomationacademy.minion, Minion's own mark (the scheming side-eye dog, Academy monochrome standard), title bar pinned to Minion, dark by default (View → Appearance records your explicit choice and later launches honor it). App data is stored separately at ~/Library/Application Support/com.detroitautomationacademy.minion. Standing features: the genuine Terminal view (View menu, Command-T) over the live hosted session, markdown routing to MacDown with the consented system default, window repair, up-arrow message history, the SDS-8 welcome. Unsigned test build; the Tachometer rig verdict is the owner's, at the Air sitting.

apps.description: Snowfell is the Detroit Automation Academy's Jira-style board application for Intel Macs running macOS High Sierra (10.13): every Academy project board in one native window. The bundled registry snapshot (v8-0041) carries 74 GitHub Projects boards and 614 items — the Academy's GitHub across the user smit4786 and the AutomatedTechnologies organization — with a portfolio rollup (health dot and an Open / Done split per board), per-board kanban whose columns are each board's own status vocabulary (data, never a hardcoded list), item detail, a roadmap over start and target dates, a command palette, an orchestration queue over a data-driven action manifest, an incidents lens for consequential matters, their evidence, and their deadlines, and the V12 Storage lens (View menu, Command-8): a multi-tenant cloud storage and content-management console over the bundled SnowfellStorageService helper, loopback-only, with content-addressed deduplication by SHA-256. Changes are staged, not narrated: moving a card, adding an item, or commenting asks in plain terms — "Move '<item>' to <status> on <board>?" — and stages the change in a queue on the Mac; the full technical record (the exact GitHub operation, its destination, the staging store) sits behind each confirmation's Details button and in the Staged Changes panel, and nothing is sent without the owner's explicit Send Pending Changes in an armed build. Board state is derived, not mirrored: a board whose items all sit in its own terminal status presents as Complete (the raw GitHub state is kept as secondary detail) whenever the loaded snapshot carries the registry's derivation (schema v9+). Snowfell reads a pinned, hash-verified snapshot of the Academy registry and works fully offline; a newer snapshot can be fetched and verified in-app before it is swapped in. GitHub write-back is compiled OFF in this build (SNOWFELL_WRITEBACK_ENABLED = 0): actions stage locally and nothing is sent. Academy-original software under the Academy License (revocable). Unsigned test build.

apps.description: Tachometer is the Detroit Automation Academy's on-device analytics application for Intel Macs running macOS High Sierra (10.13). It measures the Academy's own applications where they actually run: per-process CPU and memory, itemized by role (shell, renderer, GPU, helper), so a cost like an animated avatar's is a number read off the device, not an estimate. Samples land in a segmented, append-only store under the app's own Application Support — single writer by lock, second writer refused, never merged — with rotation and retention bounds, and the built-in budget scorer reads that stream against the estate's per-app budgets (the Minion avatar budget: at most 10% of one thread sustained), reporting PASS, FAIL, or NO DATA — unmeasured is never a silent pass. There is no network code in the app: data is generated, stored, and read on the device only. Academy-original software under the Academy License (revocable). Unsigned test build.
